_notes_landing_field: Landing fields and drop ships on the ground (owner 2026-11-17: "the landers do not return to the ship, but land in an area near the outpost to fly back up after re-fueling"; game/sim/Surface/LandingField.cs). Every colony core gets a landing field when it is placed (landed, dropped, founded): pads hexes in one cluster, the first one distance hexes from the core and the rest touching the cluster at distance or distance + 1, on passable buildable ground with no deposit, building, ruin, toxic patch or native land (fewer pads when the ground doesn't have room; of the possible clusters the one with most pads, then most on landing terrain, then the flattest). Nothing can be built on a pad, crawlers can't unfurl there, drop ships can't be ordered down onto one, and vehicles treat its middle like a building of footprint_radius (they drive round it and park toward the hex corners; footprint_radius + lanes.clearance at most 12). A drop ship that has brought something down (an orbit delivery, each ship of the first-landing convoy, each ship of an outpost drop) no longer climbs straight back: it unloads (unload_seconds after a delivery arrives; a convoy ship that carried a vehicle is ready convoy_unload_seconds after the colony's touchdown, one that only carried an outpost module module_seconds after it; ship k of a convoy stagger_seconds x k later), hops to a free pad of its owner's nearest base (hop_seconds + hop_seconds_per_tile x hexes, at most hop_max_seconds; the pad is taken from the start of the hop until lift-off), refuels there for refuel_seconds (x the world's lift-cost curve, like the fuel), then climbs back to the ship (orbit.shuttle.flight_seconds x the descent-time curve). The ship's one delivery drop ship is away for all of it. Fuel: an orbit delivery's trip fuel (orbit.shuttle.fuel x lift cost) is taken from the colony's stock when refuelling starts, not at the order (the order still needs it in stock); with none in stock the ship waits on its pad until there is. Convoy and outpost-drop ships brought their own fuel (free), but still take the refuel time. With every pad taken a landed ship waits where it unloaded; a ship still hovering on its module's cables (it never landed) and any ship of an owner with no field at all climbs straight back. Convoy ships: three bring the outpost's modules (a first landing's three also carry landing.units, one each), and every further vehicle of a first landing (a picked ship's start_units, e.g. the Cochrane's construction rover) comes down in one more ship of its own. Every number is a placeholder.
